bull_bear.body:
- Ongoing product/technology development in CIAB — e.g., deployment of a high-speed marking solution operating at 750 PPM for ECU marking, a new marking solution integrated with an air balancer, and revival of the conventional marking machines portfolio
- Diversifying customer base beyond conventional automotive components into non-automotive key accounts such as steel, pharmaceuticals and FMCG, reducing dependence on the automotive capex cycle
- Improvement in CIAB gross margins achieved through optimal utilisation of resources and effective cost controls, reinforcing product competitiveness
- Debt-free standalone and consolidated balance sheet as at March 31, 2026
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Political and global economic uncertainty — Political uncertainty or volatile economic conditions may adversely affect demand and could restrict revenue growth opportunities; mitigated only partly through diversified businesses across industries and markets and continued cost control.
- Dependence on industrial capital expenditure cycles and competitive pressure — CIAB demand and margins are exposed to global economic and geopolitical uncertainties, competitive pressure from domestic and international players, rapid technological change, and dependence on customers' industrial capex cycles.
- Input cost and currency volatility — CIAB operations were impacted during the year by cost pressure arising from currency fluctuations and higher commodity prices amid ongoing geopolitical developments.
- Legal and regulatory complexity — The Company is subject to laws across product safety, product claims, trademarks, copyright, patents, competition, employee health and safety, environment, water and air pollution, corporate governance, listing/disclosure, employment and taxes; frequent regulatory changes and multiple overlapping authorities add compliance complexity.
- Cybersecurity and IT systems dependence — Operations are increasingly dependent on IT systems; the threat of unauthorized access, misuse of sensitive information, or disruption to operations from cyber-attacks continues to increase as digital interactions with customers and suppliers grow.
- Litigation and pledged-shareholding exposure related to The Svadeshi Mills Company Limited — The Company (with Forbes Campbell Finance Limited) holds 22.7% of Svadeshi, pledged to Asia Pragati Strategic Investment Fund; a winding-up petition against Svadeshi is contested, with the Bombay High Court dismissing an Interim Application for a stay (order dated 23 February 2026) and an Appeal now reserved for order before the Division Bench.
- Real Estate segment revenue lumpiness / project concentration — Multiple key ratios (debtors turnover, interest coverage, ROE, ROCE, net capital turnover) swung sharply year-on-year mainly due to the absence of Vicinia Real Estate Project revenue/profit recognised in the prior year, indicating segment results are driven by the completion and sales-recognition timing of individual real-estate projects rather than a steady operating base.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Forbes & Company operates the Coding & Industrial Automation Business (CIAB), comprising conventional marking systems, Dot Peen Marking Systems, Laser Technologies and Industrial Project Automation, serving automotive and non-automotive manufacturers (steel, pharmaceuticals, FMCG, defence, electronics, engineering). It also develops Real Estate projects in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region (a residential project at Chandivali and a planned IT/ITES park at Wagle Estate, Thane), and holds investments in subsidiaries/joint ventures including Forbes Campbell Finance, Forbes Bumi Armada (FPSO manning services) and listed group entities Eureka Forbes and Forbes Precision Tools and Machine Parts.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Coding and Industrial Automation (CIAB):** Conventional marking systems, Dot Peen Marking Systems, Laser Technologies (CO2 and UV), Industrial Project Automation, High-speed on-the-fly marking solutions (e.g., ECU marking at 750 PPM)
- **Real Estate:** Project Vicinia, Chandivali (residential towers), Wagle Estate, Thane (planned IT/ITES park)

- Forbes Campbell Finance Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned material subsidiary; an unregistered Core Investment Company (CIC) with asset size below Rs. 100 crores, holding investments in Forbes & Company Limited, Eureka Forbes Limited, Forbes Precision Tools and Machine Parts Limited and Forbes Bumi Armada Limited.

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Concentrate on growth-oriented businesses, specifically Coding & Industrial Automation and Real Estate, following the demerger
- Further enhance the performance of laser machines and expand the product portfolio within the CO2 and UV domains to strengthen CIAB's capability to address diverse customer requirements
- Strengthen the talent pipeline through development of Graduate Engineering Trainees (GETs) to address capability gaps in PLC and software resources, while stabilizing critical design and operations positions
- Expand the customer base beyond conventional automotive components by actively developing non-automotive key accounts in steel, pharmaceuticals and FMCG, supported by new dedicated sales roles
- Continue judicious management of working capital with relentless focus on receivables, inventories and strict cost control, maintaining a debt-free balance sheet
- The Company is Debt Free as on March 31, 2026 and continues to focus on judicious management of working capital, with relentless focus on receivables, inventories and strict cost control where possible. No dividend was recommended by the Board for the year under review, though the Board has adopted a Dividend Distribution Policy (per SEBI LODR) available on the Company's website; no amount was transferred to reserves during the year.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Expansion activity is concentrated in Real Estate and in CIAB product-portfolio broadening rather than manufacturing capacity addition. In Real Estate, Project Vicinia, Chandivali has completed construction of all towers (Phase I: A, B, C, D, F; Phase II: E, G, H) with flats handed over, and the Company is completing remaining amenities/infrastructure with full Occupation Certificate expected by December 2026 (entire flat inventory sold except five flats). A second project at Wagle Estate, Thane (10,671.49 sq. metres / 2.63 acres within MIDC Industrial Area, approx. 6.2 lakh sq. ft. built-up area) is being developed as a private IT/ITES park after the Company received approval for change of land use from industrial to IT/ITES; development designs and plans are being finalized for submission to MIDC. In CIAB, expansion is product-led: enhancing laser machine performance and expanding the portfolio within the CO2 and UV domains, alongside R&D outputs such as a 200-watt Fiber laser SPM for VIN marking and an 8T roll marking machine for 155mm artillery shells. The Directors' Report states the Company's (post-demerger) operations involve low energy consumption with no major further energy-conservation measures identified, and Nil capital investment on energy-conservation equipment and Nil R&D expenditure during the year.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's GDP growth is estimated at approximately 7.4% in FY 2025-26 and expected to remain in the range of 6.5%-7.0% in FY 2026-27, driven by sustained public capital expenditure, gradual recovery in private investment and resilient consumption
- Government's continued emphasis on infrastructure development, manufacturing and digitalisation has supported investment activity and created opportunities for the Company's coding and industrial automation solutions
- The Company witnessed steady demand across its coding solutions and industrial automation businesses, supported by increasing adoption of technology and efficiency-led initiatives
- The real estate segment benefited from improved demand conditions and ongoing urbanisation
- Outlook remains cautiously optimistic; global uncertainties and input cost volatility persist as headwinds, but underlying strength of the Indian economy and continued policy focus on investment and reforms are expected to sustain growth momentum
- CIAB operations were impacted by cost pressure from currency fluctuations, higher commodity prices and ongoing geopolitical developments, while gross margins improved through optimal utilisation of resources and effective cost controls
- Growth opportunities are driven by increasing adoption of new technologies, rising demand for automation, and the need for product traceability, particularly in pharmaceuticals, defence, automotive, engineering and electronics
